h1:
Bangkok Night Markets
Where to Eat in 2026
intro: Night is when Bangkok is at its most fun. Once the sun drops and the air cools, markets across the city switch on their lights, fire up the grills, and the smell of charred prawns and grilled pork drifts out from blocks away. We've picked the markets that are actually open right now, with the standout dish at each, roughly what you'll pay, and how to get there without getting lost — because plenty of the old famous spots have already shut down.

blocks.html: First, the honest part. The Bangkok night market scene moves fast. In 2025 Jodd Fairs Rama 9, once the hottest of them all, closed for good, and The One Ratchada shut down too. So if you find an old list online and drive out only to hit a locked gate, don't be confused — we've updated this to show which ones are genuinely still running.

blocks.text: The night markets worth going to (updated 2026)

items.name: Jodd Fairs Ratchada
items.blurb: The hottest one right now, after everything was consolidated into the single Ratchada location next to Big C. The dish to get is leng saeb (volcano) — pork ribs ladled with a fiery herbal soup and piled high like a volcano. The big draw is that it's open every day, so you don't have to wait for the weekend.
items.meta: Open daily 17:00–01:00 · MRT Thailand Cultural Centre Exit 4, 3-min walk

items.name: Talad Rot Fai Srinakarin (Train Night Market)
items.blurb: The biggest night market in Bangkok, with a strong vintage-retro theme — there's a zone of classic cars, collectibles and second-hand clothes, and the food section out the back goes all in: grilled prawns, salt-crusted grilled fish, seafood everywhere. The photo spot looking down over the market from the upper level is great.
items.meta: Open Thu–Sun 17:00–01:00 · Behind Seacon Square Srinakarin, Soi 51

items.name: Liab Duan DanNeramit
items.blurb: The rising star of 2026, taking over the old Jodd Fairs DanNeramit spot. The selling point is the big fairy-tale castle that doubles as a photo backdrop. It's quieter than Jodd Fairs and more relaxed, with live music and food that's cheap and good — seafood buckets, som tam, Isaan grilled chicken, fried snacks, sushi from ฿10.
items.meta: Open daily 17:00–24:00 · BTS Ha Yaek Lat Phrao or MRT Phahon Yothin

items.name: Train Night Market Ratchada
items.blurb: The legend is back at its old spot behind Esplanade Ratchada. The highlight is the high-angle view over a sea of colourful tarpaulin tents. The food covers everything savoury and sweet, plus craft-beer bars, and a younger crowd likes coming here to hang out.
items.meta: Behind Esplanade Ratchada · MRT Thailand Cultural Centre (check opening days before you go)

blocks.title: When to go
blocks.html: Most markets open around 5pm, but the food stalls don't really all open until about 7pm onwards. If you want to walk around comfortably before the stalls get busy, go between 17:00–19:00 before the tour groups arrive. If you prefer the buzzing, fully-lit atmosphere, go from 8pm on.

blocks.text: What to order while walking the night markets

blocks.html: Walking the Bangkok night markets, there are a few things you see and just have to try — the stars people actually queue up for. We've picked them out with rough prices (food at tourist-facing markets usually runs a bit higher than the roadside stalls in the sois).

items.name: Leng Saeb (volcano)
items.blurb: Fall-apart pork ribs ladled with a fiery herbal soup and piled high like a volcano — the star of Jodd Fairs. Properly spicy, best with a side of hot sticky rice.

items.name: Giant grilled river prawns
items.blurb: Enormous grilled prawns oozing with prawn fat, dipped in a punchy seafood sauce. It's the dish everyone photographs for social media at these markets. Price depends on the size.

items.name: Boat noodles
items.blurb: Thin noodles in a rich, dark broth with pork blood, meatballs and a scatter of fried garlic. The bowls are small, so you'll happily order several — a night-market staple forever.

items.name: Seafood bucket
items.blurb: Prawns, clams, crab and corn in a prawn-fat sauce, served in a bucket and tipped out onto a tray — built for sharing with a group. It went viral straight out of these very night markets.

items.name: Som tam, grilled chicken & grilled pork neck
items.blurb: The classic Isaan combo every market has — punchy som tam, crispy-skinned grilled chicken, tender grilled pork neck, all eaten with sticky rice. Filling and good value.

items.name: Mango sticky rice
items.blurb: The dessert to finish on — sweet ripe mango with coconut-milk sticky rice and a sprinkle of beans. Nearly every market has a regular stall for it.

items.name: Pad thai with fresh prawns
items.blurb: Noodles stir-fried in a well-balanced tamarind sauce with prawns, egg and bean sprouts, topped with peanuts and a squeeze of lime — the plate almost every traveller orders.

items.name: Viral drinks (cup or jar)
items.blurb: Thick poured cocoa, Thai tea, big cups of blended fruit juice — drinks made for wandering and snapping photos. Easy to sip as you stroll.

blocks.text: Two nights, two zones (a quick plan)

blocks.html: If you only have two nights and want to make the most of the night markets, here's a route. One night stays central and easy to reach by MRT, the other heads out to the Srinakarin side to catch the biggest market.

items.note: Open Thu–Sun only, so check the day first. It's behind Seacon Square

blocks.title: Before you go
blocks.html: Bring cash — plenty of stalls still take only cash or PromptPay · wear comfortable shoes because you'll be on your feet a lot · the days are hot and the nights still muggy, so carry a sweat towel and water · some stalls sell out fast later in the night, so order from any must-try stall early.

blocks.text: Pick the market that fits your style

items.name: Easy to reach, no car
items.blurb: Jodd Fairs Ratchada or Train Night Market Ratchada — get off at MRT Thailand Cultural Centre and walk straight there. Jodd Fairs is open every day.

items.name: Want a big market for a long wander
items.blurb: Talad Rot Fai Srinakarin, the biggest in Bangkok — the place for vintage and seafood. But it's open Thu–Sun only.

items.name: Want to dodge the crowds and chill
items.blurb: Liab Duan DanNeramit is less crowded, with live music, a photo-worthy castle and cheap food.

faq.q: Which Bangkok night market is the most popular right now?
faq.a: Jodd Fairs Ratchada is the hottest in 2026, after everything was consolidated into the single Ratchada location. It's open daily 17:00–01:00 and is just a 3-minute walk from MRT Thailand Cultural Centre Exit 4. The standout dish is leng saeb (volcano).

faq.q: Are Jodd Fairs Rama 9 and The One Ratchada still open?
faq.a: No. Jodd Fairs Rama 9 closed in early 2025, and The One Ratchada shut down too. Jodd Fairs has consolidated its operation into the single Ratchada branch (next to Big C).

faq.q: How much should I budget for a night market visit?
faq.a: For grazing as you walk, 200–400 THB per person is plenty. Signature dishes like leng saeb start around ฿180, grilled prawns around ฿150–250, boat noodles ฿20–40 a bowl, and big drinks ฿35–69. Bring cash, as many stalls still don't take cards.

faq.q: Which days are the night markets open?
faq.a: Jodd Fairs Ratchada and Liab Duan DanNeramit are open every day, while Talad Rot Fai Srinakarin opens Thursday to Sunday only. Always check the opening days before you travel, as some markets change their hours often.

faq.q: What's the best time to visit a night market?
faq.a: The markets open around 5pm, but the food stalls don't all really open until about 7pm onwards. If you want to walk around comfortably before it gets busy, go between 17:00–19:00 before the tour groups arrive. If you prefer the buzzing, fully-lit atmosphere, go from 8pm on.
